symptom: ako/mxcli#819 (follow-ups of #802), measured on a blank 11.13.0 app with security on. (1) `create or modify association Crm.Lead_Order from Crm.Lead to Hr.Employee owner both` — moving a cross-module OWNER Both association's TO end from Shop.Order — printed "Modified association" and mx check reported CE0066 "Entity access is out of date" at the domain models of both Shop (old TO) and Hr (new TO); moving it to another entity of the same module, or only changing the owner through create or modify, left CE0066 at the TO module. `update security` repaired Hr but not Shop. (2) `create association … from <non-persistent> to <persistent> owner both` passed check and exec and failed CE0001 "An association between a persistable entity and a non-persistable entity must start in the non-persistable entity and have owner 'Default'."; so did a persistent FROM end under owner Default, and `alter association … set owner both`. (3) GRANT naming the TO-side member of a cross-module OWNER Both association (`read (Number, Lead_Order)`) already worked on main — fixed by 74bc820b7, verified 0 errors.
cause: (1) The cross-module OR MODIFY branch of execCreateAssociation overwrote ChildRef and owner and reconciled nothing itself; the end-of-program reconcile covered only the declaring module. And ReconcileMemberAccesses kept the old TO entity's entry even when its module was reconciled: a reference to another module's association was preserved on faith (the #758 rule for associations inherited across modules), and this one still exists, just not as a member. (2) No check or exec guard modelled CE0001.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_associations.go (OR MODIFY cross branch reconciles declaring, old TO and new TO modules via reconcileModulesAccess; refusals on create and alter set owner both); mdl/executor/validate_association_persistence.go (associationPersistenceViolation, projectEntityPersistence, storedAssociationEnds, ValidateAssociationPersistence — wired into ValidateProgram); mdl/backend/modelsdk/domainmodel_security_write.go (staleForeignRef: an existing foreign association on an entity whose generalization chain never leaves its module is stale unless collected as an incoming OWNER Both)
insight: The issue named one half of each defect. The move left a stale entry on the OLD TO module and a missing one on the NEW TO module — read the old ChildRef before overwriting it — and the CE0001 rule is two-sided: mxbuild's message (and a 4-cell measurement: NP->P default ok, NP->P both, P->NP default, P->NP both all CE0001) says FROM must be the non-persistable end AND owner Default, so refusing only `owner both` would have left the persistent-FROM case writing a broken model. Measure the whole matrix before scoping a refusal to the reported cell. For the reconcile, 'cannot be checked' was only true when the entity inherits from another module: with a module-local generalization chain the full member set is known (own + incoming OWNER Both), so anything else foreign is stale; the cross-module-inheritance control stays green. Persistability for the refusal comes from the backend (specializations resolved from their root, mendixlabs/mxcli#1600) in exec and from the script's own declarations first in check, through one predicate. A single bug-test script under-reports the move on the old binary: grants track Hr, so the end-of-program reconcile repairs the new TO module and only the old one shows.
